info.title: Cloudonym API
info.description: Multi-cloud resource naming engine. This release enables Google Cloud (gcp) only; AWS and Azure are in the rule table but not enabled, and a request for them is 400 request.provider_not_enabled with the enabled providers in supported. Generates, corrects and validates resource names, one by one or for a whole project with the naming wizard (/wizard), against each provider's physical constraints. Names from /wizard may carry a tier token (web, was) after the abbreviation and kind token, and attached resources (boot and data disks, reserved addresses) are named after their server; /generate and /names never put a tier in a name. Formulas, region codes, the zones they accept, kind tokens and every rule are in /llms.txt; the resource catalog and region table are in /catalog.json (served from the site root, not under /v1). Cloudonym does not replace the provider's final verdict: it checks only the reserved words and patterns that the official documents state. Successful responses of /generate, /names, /wizard, /validate and /health carry version { engine, rules }; failures and /events do not. Every failure has the ErrorResponse shape; an unknown /v1 path or method returns 404 with code request.not_found. PASS / `valid: true` means the name satisfies the documented naming checks of this rules revision (length, pattern, reserved words). It does not mean the name is available or that you may create it — uniqueness, permissions, quotas and organisation policy are not checked. Generated names are not guaranteed unique: shortening can map two different contexts to the same name.

post.description: Generates names and standard labels for every resource type of the requested providers from five context values. Names that cannot fit even after shortening are returned with valid=false and the reasons; nothing is silently truncated. Every violation, step and note is a Message: branch on code, show message to people. This is the catalogue: rules that need a kind (resource policies) come back valid=false here (name.kind_required); use /names with kind for them.

At most the first 50 errors are listed; when there are more, the last entry is request.errors_truncated with params.shown (50) and params.total (the number of errors found)

post.summary: Generate names for the resources you pick
post.description: Generates names for the selected resource types of one provider, count names each (sequence 01..99) or one per role, with an optional kind (a value name such as POSTGRES) whose short token goes right after the abbreviation. One request stands for one instance of each parent scope (one resource group, one project, one VPC): two items of the same kind of resource with the same name are each marked valid=false with name.conflict, and conflicts lists each collision once. Items that fail or collide are still returned with the reasons (status 200). Every violation, step and note is a Message: branch on code, show message to people.

200.description: Names for the selected resources, in request order then sequence order. data.<provider>.valid is false when any item is invalid or collides

400.description: Body is not JSON or not an object, provider is unknown or not enabled yet (request.provider_not_enabled; supported lists the enabled providers), context is invalid (including an owner, system or purpose longer than 64 characters, or an env or region longer than 1024), rules_version is not a string, or resources is invalid: not an array, empty, more than 200 items, an item that is not an object, an unknown type (supported lists the resource types), a duplicate type, count not an integer from 1 to 99, count above 1 or a role on a rule that takes none, a role not matching ^[a-z0-9]{2,16}$, a kind on a rule that takes none (selection.kind_not_supported), a kind that is not one of the rule's values (selection.unknown_kind; params.supported lists them), no kind on a rule that needs one (selection.kind_required; params.supported), or more than 200 names in total (selection.* codes)

post.summary: Name a whole project: project-level resources and one or more services
post.description: The naming wizard. One request is one GCP project: the project ID (always the first item), project-level resources (project_picks: network, firewall rules, Cloud Router, Cloud NAT) and, per service (purpose), the resources picked from presets or by rule id. Servers keep their sequence number (instances[].seq), so removing server 01 does not rename server 02. A server can carry attached resources (boot disk, data disks, a static external or internal address) whose names are the server name plus a suffix (-boot, -data-01, -ip, -ipi); they are never shortened. Items are returned in order: project level, then each service, each parent followed by its attached resources. Item keys are structured paths (service/shop/compute_instance/-/web/01/data/01). Items that fail or collide are still returned with the reasons (status 200). The response is reproduced by repeating the same wizard request with its rules_version; /names is a separate, flat endpoint.

200.description: Names for the whole project, in structured-key order. data.<provider>.valid is false when any item is invalid or collides

400.description: Body is not JSON or not an object, provider is unknown or not enabled yet, project is not an object, a context value or purpose is invalid or too long (field project.owner, services[1].purpose ...), or the wizard plan is invalid (wizard.* and selection.* codes). field is the request path of the offending element, in request names: services[1].picks[0].instances[1].attach.data[0], project_picks[2], services[1]. Errors about the whole plan (wizard.empty, wizard.too_many_services, wizard.too_many_names, selection.not_array for services or project_picks) have no field. At most the first 50 errors are listed; when there are more, the last entry is request.errors_truncated with params.shown (50) and params.total (the number of errors found)

env.description: Canonical: prod, stg, dev, sbx, qa, uat, test, perf, dr. Common aliases are accepted and normalised (prd, production, live -> prod; staging -> stg; development -> dev; sandbox -> sbx; quality -> qa; acceptance -> uat; testing, tst -> test; performance, load -> perf; disaster, recovery -> dr).

region.description: A region or a zone of the provider, by name or by code (asia-northeast3, asia-northeast3-a, ane3, ane3a), or global. Names carry the region code (ane3); a zone name is accepted and resolved to its region, so zonal resources are named like regional ones. Country values and region names of another provider are 400 context.value_unsupported with candidates in supported. The region table is in /llms.txt. Multi-region and dual-region locations (US, EU, ASIA, ASIA1, EUR4, EUR5, EUR7, EUR8, NAM4; by name or code, any case) are taken only by the resource types that support them: storage_bucket takes all nine, bigquery_dataset takes US and EU; names carry the lower-case code (us). A location is accepted only when every requested type that carries a region token takes it, otherwise 400 context.location_unsupported — always on /v1/generate, which names every type.

providers.description: Omit for every enabled provider (only gcp for now; aws and azure are planned). Must be non-empty when present. A known provider that is not enabled yet is 400 request.provider_not_enabled.

rules_version.description: Optional pin to a rules revision (YYYY-MM-DD.N). If it differs from the current revision the API answers 409 instead of returning names that may differ. Not a string -> 400.

data.description: provider -> resource_type -> ResourceItem. The provider set equals the requested providers.

generated_labels.description: provider -> standard tags/labels (owner, system, purpose, environment, managed_by)

label_violations.description: provider -> label values over the provider's limit or with characters the provider rejects (values are never truncated)

label_transformed.description: provider -> label values changed to fit the provider's character rules (GCP)

transformed.description: Context values normalised from aliases (context.normalized, e.g. env 'production' -> 'prod')

name.description: Final name. Empty when a required token became empty after normalisation.

valid.description: PASS / `valid: true` means the name satisfies the documented naming checks of this rules revision (length, pattern, reserved words). It does not mean the name is available or that you may create it — uniqueness, permissions, quotas and organisation policy are not checked. Generated names are not guaranteed unique: shortening can map two different contexts to the same name.

is_truncated.description: Optional tokens were dropped or tokens were shortened to fit

is_transformed.description: Characters were changed by normalisation or separators were removed

original.description: Name assembled before normalisation and shortening

violations.description: Why the name is invalid (empty when valid)

warnings.description: Present only when there is one: the name has a form the provider's documentation advises against but does not forbid (for example `warning.arn_suffix_lookalike`). It never changes `valid` (D112).

example.message: Ends with a hyphen and six characters, like the random suffix Secrets Manager adds to the ARN; AWS advises against it because a search by partial ARN can then give unexpected results. The name is accepted

steps.description: Shortening and transformation steps in order (step.token_dropped, step.abbreviated, step.budget_shortened, step.normalized, step.separator_removed)

resources.description: The resource types to name, each at most once. The total number of names (sum of count) is at most 200. The limits are for one screen and one share link; they do not bound the response size.

type.description: A resource_type of the provider (see /llms.txt Resource tree)

count.description: Only on rules with a sequence number (input count). Default 1

role.description: Only on role rules (input role). Default sync

kind.description: Only on rules with a kind table (see /llms.txt Kind tokens): a value name of that rule, such as POSTGRES or snapshot-schedule, not the token. The value that is the provider default for that scope adds no token. Required on resource_policy

rules_version.description: Optional pin to a rules revision (YYYY-MM-DD.N). If it differs from the current revision the API answers 409 instead of returning names that may differ. Not a string -> 400.

data.description: provider -> NamesProviderResult. Exactly one key: the requested provider.

valid.description: true only when every item is valid (after name.conflict is applied)

conflicts.description: One name.conflict per collision (params.name, params.keys). The same message is also in the violations of each colliding item

NameItem.description: One generated name of /names: a ResourceItem with the item key, resource type, sequence or role, kind, placement scope and uniqueness

key.description: Unique within the response: resource_type_seq (count rules), resource_type_role (role rules) or resource_type (rules with no input)

role.description: Present on role rules: the requested role or the default sync

kind.description: Present when the item asked for a kind: the value name as sent

kind_token.description: Present when the kind puts a token in the name (absent for the provider default of that scope)

scope.description: scope is the placement scope: the parent the resource is created in (a scope id such as azure:resource_group). It says where the name lives, not that the provider enforces uniqueness there; see uniqueness.

uniqueness.description: uniqueness "csp" means the provider requires the name to be unique within its scope; "none" (AWS Name tags) means the provider does not enforce uniqueness at all. Cloudonym compares names only with each other inside one request (name.conflict), never with resources that already exist.

pattern.description: Provider's physical rule (regular expression source). Rebuild with new RegExp(pattern, pattern_flags).

pattern_flags.description: RegExp flags for pattern ('u' for Unicode classes, else empty)

allowed.description: Character set Cloudonym uses when generating (house style)

doc_url.description: Official document the numbers come from

notes.description: Notes on the rule, e.g. where a limit is deliberately conservative or reserved words apply (note.* codes). Always present, may be empty

Message.description: One reason, step, note or error. code is stable for machines; message is English text for people and may change between releases.

field.description: Context field (owner ...), token name, label key or request field (provider, providers[1], rules_version ...) the message is about

params.description: Values used in message. User values (from, to, value) are display strings: cut to 40 characters followed by … in failure responses (params.value, params.requested and the message built from them), non-strings shown as JSON; control, bidirectional and zero-width characters are shown as \uXXXX text in params and message

message.example: Name is 34 characters long; the maximum is 30

Version.description: engine = Cloudonym engine version; rules = rules revision (YYYY-MM-DD.N). A different rules revision may give a different name, verdict, suggestion or label for the same input.

resource_type.description: One of the provider's resource types; an unknown value returns 400 with the supported list

name.description: Longer than 1024 characters returns 400. Up to 1024, a name over the rule's max_length is judged by the engine (valid=false with a length violation).

example.message: Ends with a hyphen and six characters, like the random suffix Secrets Manager adds to the ARN; AWS advises against it because a search by partial ARN can then give unexpected results. The name is accepted

suggested_name.description: Present only when the name is invalid and a fix is possible

suggested_warnings.description: Present only when `suggested_name` is present and has a form the documentation advises against: the warnings of the suggested name, not of the name you sent (D112).

target.description: Which copy button succeeded (plan-json: the wizard's Save plan download, D100). Required when event is ui_copy (missing is 400 request.field_missing, unknown is 400 request.value_unsupported, both with field target); ignored for the other events. The copied text, the item key and the resource type are never sent.

chip_rules.description: Rule ids of the resource kinds picked in the wizard with a preset chip (the serverless rule when serverless is on). Read only on ui_generate and ignored for the other events. Only ids of the rule table are kept; a value that is not an array of strings, or is longer than the number of rules, is dropped without an error. Context values, service names, tiers and roles are never sent.

custom_rules.description: Rule ids of the resource kinds picked in the wizard with Custom. Read only on ui_generate and ignored for the other events. Only ids of the rule table are kept; a value that is not an array of strings, or is longer than the number of rules, is dropped without an error. Context values, service names, tiers and roles are never sent.

ErrorResponse.description: Every failure (400, 403, 409, 413, 429, 500) has this shape. A /wizard or /generate 400 lists at most the first 50 errors; when there are more, a last entry with code request.errors_truncated and params { shown, total } says how many were left out. Other routes list every error. User values echoed in params.value and params.requested (and the message) are cut to 40 characters followed by …; supported is never cut

example.message: env 'preprod' is not supported (prod, stg, dev, sbx, qa, uat, test, perf, dr)

supported.description: Accepted values, present when a provider, resource_type, resources type, event or providers entry is unknown, or when providers is not a non-empty array (request.providers_not_array, request.providers_empty)

CatalogResponse.description: The resource catalog and region table of the enabled providers, with what a client needs to build a wizard plan: each rule's input kind, tier slot and locations, the wizard presets, the attachment table and the request limits. Generated from catalog/*.json and the engine's tables in the repository, the same data the engine and /llms.txt use.

providers.description: Keyed by enabled provider (gcp in this release)

meta.description: Source versions the catalog was checked against (gcloud, Terraform provider, discovery revision)

rules.description: Rule id -> { scope, regionToken (none or region), kinds? { default, allowed }, input, tier, locations? }. A row with several rules asks for the scope; each rule is one resource_type of /v1/names and one rule of a wizard pick

input.description: What a pick of this rule takes: count (numbered servers, instances[] in /v1/wizard), role (one role value) or none

tier.description: Whether the name has a tier slot (a pick may send tier)

locations.description: Values a wizard pick may send as location (multi-region and dual-region names, or regional for a secret). Absent when the rule takes no location

slug.description: The abbreviation in the name and why it was chosen

kind.description: Kind value name -> token (null = no token), the values that add no token and the source

aliases.description: Search terms: Terraform type, gcloud group, product name, earlier abbreviation

regions.description: Regions with their code and zones

presets.description: Wizard presets (POST /v1/wizard pick.preset). Empty for a provider without the wizard

tier.description: The tier used when the pick sends none

tier_choices.description: Tiers offered on the screen; the first is the default

kind.description: Fixed kind; another kind is wizard.preset_kind_fixed

ha.description: The pick may send ha: true with at least min_instances servers

serverless.description: Rules the pick may send as serverless

default_attach.description: Attachments the screen turns on for a new server (not added by the API)

attachments.description: Resources attached to a server slot (instances[].attach): parent rule, attach key, child rule and whether the child is numbered (data disks)

limits.description: Request limits and value patterns, for a client to check before sending. The API's answer is the verdict

WizardRequest.description: One project. project_picks and services may each be empty or omitted, but not both (wizard.empty)

project.description: The project context: the four values without purpose. Each service adds its purpose

env.description: Canonical: prod, stg, dev, sbx, qa, uat, test, perf, dr. Common aliases are accepted and normalised (prd, production, live -> prod; staging -> stg; development -> dev; sandbox -> sbx; quality -> qa; acceptance -> uat; testing, tst -> test; performance, load -> perf; disaster, recovery -> dr).

region.description: A region or a zone of the provider, by name or by code (asia-northeast3, asia-northeast3-a, ane3, ane3a), or global. Names carry the region code (ane3); a zone name is accepted and resolved to its region, so zonal resources are named like regional ones. Country values and region names of another provider are 400 context.value_unsupported with candidates in supported. The region table is in /llms.txt. The project region is a single region: a multi-region or dual-region location here is 400 context.location_unsupported; give it per pick in location instead.

project_id_suffix.description: Optional suffix appended to the project ID (platform-billing-prod-team1), so a predictable ID can still be unique. Same rules as a tier: 2-16 lowercase letters or digits, not a reserved word (400 wizard.invalid_project_id_suffix, wizard.project_id_suffix_reserved). It is never shortened; the item key stays project/-/project_id/-/-/-. Project IDs are unique across Google Cloud and cannot be reused; Cloudonym does not check whether an ID is free.

project_picks.description: Project-level resources (no purpose in the name): rules placed in the project, its global or regional scope, such as vpc, subnet and firewall. At most 40

services.description: At most 20 services. purpose is the service name and namespace; after cleaning it must be non-empty, unique and not project

rules_version.description: Optional pin to a rules revision (YYYY-MM-DD.N). If it differs from the current revision the API answers 409 instead of returning names that may differ. Not a string -> 400.

environments.description: Ignored by the API. A plan file saved from the wizard (Save plan, D100) is this request body plus this list when the plan has two or more environments; project.env is the first. The API names project.env only, so send one request per environment with project.env set to each value.

WizardPick.description: One resource line: a preset or a rule. The same (rule, tier, role) may appear once per service (wizard.duplicate_pick)

preset.description: A preset id: web, was, bastion, intweb, intwas, file, db, object, run, sa, secret, gke, wip, bq, ar, topic, sub, dlq, dlqsub, build, cron, runjob, redis, worker, raw, ingest, appdata, ip, ig, bs, hc, url, cert, thps, fwd, urlredir, thp, fwdredir, neg, bb, vpc, subnet, firewall, router, nat, psa. null or omitted for a custom pick by rule. The presets are listed in /llms.txt Wizard presets

rule.description: A rule id (gcp.run_service) when preset is null. gcp.project_id is always included and cannot be picked (wizard.reserved_pick)

tier.description: The tier token placed after the abbreviation and kind token, before the sequence (billing-shop-prod-ane3-gce-web-01). On rules with a sequence number, and on Google Cloud rules with neither a sequence number nor a role, where it goes right after the abbreviation (platform-billing-shop-prod-ane3-gcs-uploads); never on role rules. Overrides the preset tier. Abbreviations, kind tokens, environment values and region codes are reserved (wizard.tier_reserved)

role.description: Only on role rules, as on /names

kind.description: A kind value name, as on /names

ha.description: High availability: only on the web and was presets as virtual machines; needs at least 2 servers (wizard.count_below_min)

serverless.description: Run the web or was preset on a serverless rule instead of a virtual machine: gcp.cloud_function or gcp.run_service

location.description: A multi-region or dual-region location for this pick, by name or code (US, us, ASIA1). Only on rules that take one: storage_bucket (US, EU, ASIA, ASIA1, EUR4, EUR5, EUR7, EUR8, NAM4) and bigquery_dataset (US, EU). The name carries its code in the region slot (…-prod-us-gcs). Omitted: the project region. On secret picks the only value is regional (D79): omitted, the secret is global and its name has no region token; regional puts the project region in its name (…-prod-ane3-secret-01), and is 400 wizard.location_needs_region when the project region is global. Anything else is 400 wizard.invalid_location with the accepted locations in params.supported.

instances.description: One slot per server (rules with a sequence number only). Required on those rules

id.description: Slot id, unique within the pick (used by share links)

seq.description: The sequence number in the name, unique within the pick

attach.description: Attached resources (virtual machines only): boot disk, data disks, static external (ip) and internal (ipi) address

WizardItem.description: One generated name of /wizard: a NameItem with a structured key, the namespace, and for attached resources the parent key and suffix kind

key.description: Structured key, unique within the response: <level>/<service>/<resource_type>/<kind|->/<tier|->/<seq|role|-> for a parent, where kind is the kind token in the name or - (project/-/vpc_network/-/-/01, project/-/subnet/proxy/-/01, service/shop/compute_instance/-/web/01), followed by /<attach>/<seq|-> for an attached resource (service/shop/compute_instance/-/web/01/data/01)

namespace.description: project for project-level items, otherwise the cleaned purpose of the service

parent.description: Present on attached resources: the key of the parent item

attach.description: Present on attached resources: the suffix kind

tier.description: Present when the item carries a tier token

role.description: Present on role rules: the requested role or the default sync

kind.description: Present when the item asked for a kind: the value name as sent

kind_token.description: Present when the kind puts a token in the name (absent for the provider default of that scope)

scope.description: scope is the placement scope: the parent the resource is created in (a scope id such as azure:resource_group). It says where the name lives, not that the provider enforces uniqueness there; see uniqueness.

uniqueness.description: uniqueness "csp" means the provider requires the name to be unique within its scope; "none" (AWS Name tags) means the provider does not enforce uniqueness at all. Cloudonym compares names only with each other inside one request (name.conflict), never with resources that already exist.

name.description: Final name. Empty when a required token became empty after normalisation.

valid.description: PASS / `valid: true` means the name satisfies the documented naming checks of this rules revision (length, pattern, reserved words). It does not mean the name is available or that you may create it — uniqueness, permissions, quotas and organisation policy are not checked. Generated names are not guaranteed unique: shortening can map two different contexts to the same name.

is_truncated.description: Optional tokens were dropped or tokens were shortened to fit

is_transformed.description: Characters were changed by normalisation or separators were removed

original.description: Name assembled before normalisation and shortening

violations.description: Why the name is invalid (empty when valid)

warnings.description: Present only when there is one: the name has a form the provider's documentation advises against but does not forbid (for example `warning.arn_suffix_lookalike`). It never changes `valid` (D112).

example.message: Ends with a hyphen and six characters, like the random suffix Secrets Manager adds to the ARN; AWS advises against it because a search by partial ARN can then give unexpected results. The name is accepted

steps.description: Shortening and transformation steps in order (step.token_dropped, step.abbreviated, step.budget_shortened, step.normalized, step.separator_removed)

valid.description: true only when every item is valid (after name.conflict is applied)

conflicts.description: One name.conflict per collision across the whole project (params.name, params.keys). The same message is also in the violations of each colliding item

generated_labels.description: provider -> namespace -> standard labels. project has owner, system, environment and managed_by; each service adds purpose

label_violations.description: provider -> label values over the limit or with rejected characters. field is <namespace>.<label key> (project.owner, shop.purpose)

label_transformed.description: provider -> label values changed to fit the character rules. field is <namespace>.<label key>

transformed.description: Context values normalised from aliases (context.normalized, e.g. env 'production' -> 'prod')

data.description: provider -> WizardProviderResult. Exactly one key: the requested provider.
